text:
Alice Chen: CI flagged a new high-severity SAST finding on PR #2148, looks like an unsafe deserialization in payment-service.
Raj Patel: saw it, triage in progress. getting a repro locally now.
scanner-bot: SAST report (critical) — CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data. File: payment-service/src/main/java/com/redwood/pay/DeserializeUtil.java. Confidence: high. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/sast/2148/report
Maya Ortiz: tagging infra/security: this touches KMS-wrapped tokens in the deserializer. Might be risky to hotfix without rotating keys.
Samir Kaur: can you paste the stack snippet?
Alice Chen: paste: ```java
Object obj = mapper.readValue(payload, Object.class); // <- user-controlled payload
```
Raj Patel: repro notes — if attacker controls payload they can cause arbitrary class loading via polymorphic types. We need to block polymorphic deserialization or validate schema.
Maya Ortiz: agree. short-term mitigation: disable polymorphic type handling and add a deserialization whitelist at the callsite. Long-term: add a static check to SAST policies for use of mapper.readValue(Object.class).
Samir Kaur: is this definitely exploitable in production? the PR only touches feature-flagged paths.
Alice Chen: production logs show ~20k calls/day to that endpoint. Feature flag is on for 35% of traffic in prod.
security-oncall: escalate — creating incident INF-492. Assigning to oncall and payment-service owner.
Raj Patel: I'll open a follow-up PR to add the whitelist and disable polymorphic typing. Will mark as hotfix.
Maya Ortiz: we need to consider KMS access patterns: the deserializer receives a payload that is KMS-encrypted upstream then decrypted here. If we change deserialization, we must ensure KMS DECRYPT IAM doesn't broaden.
Samir Kaur: request: can security get an audit log of KMS decrypts for this service last 48h? I want to confirm no anomalous decrypts.
Maya Ortiz: filing the KMS audit request now — ticket CLOUD-321. Linking logs to the incident.
scanner-bot: DAST run queued for payment-service on deploy-preview-2148.
Alice Chen: for PR flow, we need two things: 1) emergency code change + regression test, 2) SAST policy update so future PRs block similar patterns.
Raj Patel: code patch: ```diff
- Object obj = mapper.readValue(payload, Object.class);
+ mapper.disable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES);
+ mapper.activateDefaultTyping(NONE); // remove default polymorphic typing
+ PaymentPayload obj = mapper.readValue(payload, PaymentPayload.class);
```
Samir Kaur: please don't commit 'activateDefaultTyping(NONE)' — that's misleading. Better to remove any calls to enableDefaultTyping and explicitly use typed reads.
Raj Patel: yep will do typed reads.
Maya Ortiz: on RBAC: security team is asking for a temporary permission to approve the emergency PR in the repo settings (bypass codeowner) to land the hotfix quickly. Current policy requires codeowner approval from infra which is slow.
Alice Chen: what are the audit implications of giving that permission? we need full traceability.
security-oncall: we can grant "emergency-merge" role scoped to this repo for 2 hours with audit logging enabled. All merges will be recorded to the audit log (who, when, commit). Recommend using short-lived token via SSO.
Samir Kaur: sounds OK if it's limited and audited. Please record the reason in the audit entry and notify infra channel.
Maya Ortiz: also we should rotate the service KMS key used for that feature after the hotfix lands, since payloads may have been exfiltrated. Rotate with staged rollout to avoid breaking consumers.
Alice Chen: agree. plan: hotfix PR -> canary deploy to 5% -> monitor logs + DAST -> full rollout -> KMS key rotation with backward-compat window.
Raj Patel: ETA on hotfix PR — 30m. Will include regression unit + integration test and note the security rationale in the PR body and link INF-492.
security-oncall: adding required checklist for the PR: 
- link to incident INF-492
- explanation of exploitability and mitigation
- unit/integration tests
- owner for KMS rotation (Maya)
- deployment canary plan
Maya Ortiz: I'll coordinate KMS rotation and prepare Cloud Audit exports.
Samir Kaur: another ask — can eng-security propose a suppression policy for the SAST runner? We keep seeing low-value alerts for test-only mocks, but we must preserve high-confidence checks like this one.
Alice Chen: can we add an allowlist that is repo-pattern-scoped + requires security approval to add entries?
security-oncall: yes — new workflow: suppression entries go through a small UI form + require 2 security approvals and are recorded in audit logs. They are timeboxable (e.g., 30 days) and auto-expire. Implementing as infra ticket INF-500.
Raj Patel: once hotfix merged, please re-run full SAST and attach new report to INF-492.
scanner-bot: SAST full-run queued after merge.
Maya Ortiz: final notes for postmortem: root cause = risky polymorphic deserialization + insufficient SAST rule coverage for typed-read enforcement. Action items: update SAST rules, implement suppression governance, RBAC temporary approval flow, KMS rotation playbook, and add DAST smoke to PR pipeline.
Alice Chen: thanks team. I'll update the incident and ping legal for disclosure review if we find evidence of exploitation. :thumbsup:
Raj Patel: merged hotfix at 1805001355 with emergency-merge token (audit id AU-7789).
security-oncall: confirmed hotfix deployed to canary at 1805001450. No anomalous decrypts observed in audit logs in that window.
Maya Ortiz: started KMS rotation job at 1805001600, will monitor for failures.
Samir Kaur: closing thread for now, keeping INF-492 open until postmortem is done.
Alice Chen: thanks everyone.
